name: Stovetop mac and cheese
steps: Boil the macaroni in well-salted water for 1 minute less than the package says, then drain.
In the same pot, melt the butter over medium heat, whisk in the flour and cook 1 minute, stirring.
Slowly whisk in the milk and cook 4–5 minutes, stirring often, until it bubbles gently and thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Turn the heat to low, stir in the cheese a handful at a time until melted, then add the mustard if using.
Stir the pasta back in, season with salt and pepper, and serve right away.

name: Grilled cheese
steps: Spread the butter on one side of each bread slice.
Place one slice butter-side down in a nonstick pan, top with the cheese, then the second slice butter-side up.
Cook over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes until the bottom is golden, then flip.
Cook another 2–3 minutes until the second side is golden and the cheese is melted. Cut in half and serve.

name: Tomato soup

ingredients.note: use vegetable broth to keep it vegetarian

steps: Melt the butter in a pot over medium heat, add the onion and cook 5–6 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the canned tomatoes, broth and sugar; bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer 15 minutes.
Blend until smooth with a stick blender (or carefully in a blender in batches with the lid vented).
Stir in the cream if using, season with salt and pepper, and serve hot.

name: Sloppy joes
steps: Cook the ground beef, onion and bell pepper in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 7–8 minutes, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and the beef reaches 160°F.
Spoon off any excess fat.
Stir in the ketchup, brown sugar, mustard and 1/4 cup water; simmer on low for 5–10 minutes until thick. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon onto toasted bread and serve.

name: Patty melt
steps: Melt 1 tbsp butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion 10 minutes, stirring, until soft and golden; set aside.
Shape the ground beef into 2 thin oval patties about the size of the bread and season with salt and pepper.
Cook the patties in the same skillet over medium-high heat 3–4 minutes per side until they reach 160°F.
Build each sandwich: bread, cheese slice, patty, onions, cheese slice, bread.
Wipe the pan, melt the remaining butter over medium-low heat and cook the sandwiches 2–3 minutes per side until the bread is golden and the cheese melts.

name: Meatloaf
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with foil.

In a large bowl, mix the egg, breadcrumbs and milk; let sit 2 minutes. Add the ground beef, onion, garlic powder, 2 tbsp of the ketchup, the salt and some pepper, and mix gently with your hands until just combined.
Shape into a loaf about 9 by 5 inches on the baking sheet.
Stir the remaining ketchup with the brown sugar and spread it over the top.
Bake 55–65 minutes until the center reaches 160°F on a thermometer. Rest 10 minutes before slicing.

name: Cottage pie
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Cover the potatoes with salted water, boil 15 minutes until fork-tender, drain, and mash with the butter, milk, salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, cook the ground beef, onion and carrots in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 8–10 minutes, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F. Spoon off excess fat.
Stir in the tomato paste and flour and cook 1 minute, then add the broth and simmer 5 minutes until thickened. Stir in the peas and season.
Spread the beef mixture in a 2-quart baking dish and spoon the mashed potatoes over the top, roughing it up with a fork.
Bake 20–25 minutes until bubbling and the top is golden. Rest 5 minutes before serving.

name: Chicken noodle soup
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat; cook the onion, carrots and celery 5–6 minutes until starting to soften.
Add the broth, italian seasoning and whole chicken breasts. Bring to a boil, then lower to a gentle simmer and cook 15–20 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F.
Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks and set aside.
Bring the soup back to a boil, add the noodles and cook according to the package, about 6–8 minutes, until tender.
Stir the chicken back in, season with salt and pepper, and top with herbs if you like.

name: One-pot chicken and rice
steps: Season the chicken thighs with the paprika, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large lidded pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken 3 minutes per side; move to a plate (it will finish cooking later).
Lower to medium, add the onion and cook 4 minutes, then the garlic for 30 seconds. Stir in the rice for 1 minute.
Pour in the broth, scraping up the browned bits, and bring to a boil. Nestle the chicken on top, cover, and cook on low for 18–20 minutes until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 165°F.
Scatter the peas over, cover again off the heat for 5 minutes, then fluff and serve.

name: Sheet-pan chicken and vegetables
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a large sheet pan with foil or parchment.
Toss the potatoes with 1 tbsp oil and a pinch of salt, spread on the pan and roast 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, toss the chicken, broccoli and bell pepper with the remaining oil, italian seasoning, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Add them to the pan in a single layer (use two pans if crowded) and roast 15–20 minutes more until the potatoes are golden and the chicken reaches 165°F.

name: Sheet-pan sausage and potatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a large sheet pan.
Toss the potatoes with the oil, paprika, garlic powder, salt and pepper; spread out and roast 20 minutes.
Add the sausage, bell pepper and onion to the pan, toss with the potatoes, and spread back into one layer.
Roast 20–25 minutes more, stirring once, until the potatoes are golden and crisp at the edges and the sausage reaches 160°F (fully cooked smoked sausage just needs to be hot).

name: Sheet-pan salmon and green beans
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a sheet pan.
Toss the green beans with 1 tbsp oil, the garlic, salt and pepper, spread on the pan and roast 5 minutes.
Push the beans to the sides, place the salmon in the middle, brush with the remaining oil, season, and top with lemon slices.
Roast 12–15 minutes until the salmon is opaque and flakes easily with a fork (145°F). Squeeze the remaining lemon over and serve.

name: Loaded baked potatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Prick the potatoes a few times with a fork, rub with oil and salt, and bake directly on the rack 50–60 minutes until a knife slides in easily.
Meanwhile, cook the bacon in a skillet over medium heat 8–10 minutes, turning, until crisp; drain on paper towels and crumble.
Split the hot potatoes open, fluff the insides with a fork, and add the butter if using, salt and pepper.
Top with the cheese, sour cream, bacon and green onions, and serve.

name: Creamy potato soup

ingredients.note: use vegetable broth to keep it vegetarian

steps: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion 5 minutes until soft; add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir 1 minute, then slowly whisk in the broth.
Add the potatoes, bring to a boil, then simmer 15–20 minutes until very tender.
Mash some of the potatoes right in the pot (or blend half) to thicken, then stir in the milk and heat through without boiling.
Season with salt and pepper and top with cheese and green onions if you like.

name: BLT
steps: Lay the bacon in a cold skillet, set over medium heat and cook 8–10 minutes, turning, until crisp. Drain on paper towels.
Toast the bread and spread one side of each slice with mayo.
Layer lettuce, tomato slices (with a little pepper) and 4 slices of bacon on two pieces of toast, top with the rest, and cut in half.

name: Tuna melt
steps: Mix the tuna with the mayo, mustard, celery if using, and a little pepper.
Butter one side of each bread slice. Place two slices butter-side down and top each with a cheese slice, half the tuna, another cheese slice and the remaining bread, butter-side up.
Cook in a skillet over medium-low heat 3–4 minutes per side until the bread is golden and the cheese has melted.

name: Chicken Caesar-style wrap
steps: Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken 5–7 minutes per side until it reaches 165°F; rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Whisk the garlic, mayo, lemon juice, half the parmesan and plenty of pepper into a dressing.
Toss the lettuce with the dressing and the remaining parmesan.
Divide the salad and chicken between the tortillas, fold in the sides, roll up tightly and cut in half.

name: Egg salad sandwich
steps: Put the eggs in a pot, cover with cold water by an inch and bring to a boil over high heat.
Turn off the heat, cover, and let sit 11 minutes so the yolks are fully set and firm. Move the eggs to ice water for 5 minutes, then peel.
Chop the eggs and mix with the mayo, mustard, salt and pepper.
Spread on two slices of bread, add lettuce if using, and top with the remaining bread.

name: Chicken salad
steps: Put the chicken in a pot, cover with salted water and bring to a boil; reduce to a gentle simmer and cook 12–15 minutes until it reaches 165°F.
Let the chicken cool 10 minutes, then dice or shred it.
Mix the mayo, lemon juice, mustard, salt and pepper in a bowl; fold in the chicken, celery and green onions if using.
Serve on bread as sandwiches or over lettuce. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

name: Pork chops with apples
steps: Pat the pork chops dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chops 4–5 minutes per side until golden and they reach 145°F. Move to a plate and rest 3 minutes.
Lower the heat to medium, add the butter, apples and onion and cook 5–6 minutes, stirring, until softened.
Stir in the brown sugar, cinnamon and 2 tbsp water and cook 1 minute until glossy. Spoon the apples over the pork chops to serve.

name: Garlic butter steak

ingredients.note: 8–10 oz each, about 1 inch thick (sirloin or ribeye)

steps: Take the steaks out of the fridge 20 minutes ahead, pat dry and season well with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy skillet over high heat until it just smokes, add the steaks and sear 3–4 minutes without moving until a deep golden crust forms.
Flip, lower the heat to medium, and add the butter, garlic and herbs if using. Tilt the pan and spoon the foaming butter over the steaks for 3–4 minutes.
Cook to 145°F for medium (USDA-recommended), or 130–135°F if you prefer medium-rare. Rest 5 minutes, slice against the grain and pour the garlic butter over.

name: Honey mustard chicken
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and lightly oil a baking dish.
Whisk the honey, mustard, oil and garlic powder together.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper, place in the dish and pour the sauce over, turning to coat.
Bake 20–25 minutes, spooning sauce over halfway, until the chicken reaches 165°F. Rest 5 minutes and serve with the pan sauce.

name: Stuffed bell peppers
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Stand the bell peppers upright in a baking dish (trim the bottoms slightly if they wobble).
Cook the ground beef and onion in a skillet over medium-high heat 7–8 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F; add the garlic for 30 seconds and spoon off excess fat.
Stir in the canned tomatoes, rice, italian seasoning, salt and pepper, and half the cheese.
Pack the filling into the peppers, add 1/4 cup water to the dish, cover with foil and bake 30 minutes.
Uncover, top with the remaining cheese and bake 10 minutes more until the peppers are tender and the cheese is melted.

name: Turkey meatballs
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a sheet pan with parchment or lightly oiled foil.
In a bowl, gently mix the ground turkey, breadcrumbs, egg, parmesan, garlic, italian seasoning, salt and pepper until just combined.
Roll into 1 1/2-inch balls (about 16) and place on the pan.
Bake 16–20 minutes until lightly browned and the centers reach 165°F.
Serve as is, or simmer in warm pasta sauce for a few minutes and serve over pasta or in sandwiches.

name: Chili mac

ingredients.note: drained and rinsed (kidney beans also work)

steps: In a large pot over medium-high heat, cook the ground beef and onion 7–8 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F. Spoon off excess fat.
Stir in the garlic, chili powder and cumin and cook 30 seconds.
Add the canned tomatoes, beans and broth and bring to a boil.
Stir in the macaroni, cover, and simmer on medium-low 10–12 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the pasta is tender and most of the liquid is absorbed.
Season with salt, stir in half the cheese, and top with the rest. Cover 2 minutes to melt, then serve.

name: Crispy baked fish

ingredients.note: 4 cod or tilapia fillets, patted dry

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with lightly oiled foil.
Set out three shallow dishes: the flour seasoned with salt and pepper; the egg beaten with 1 tbsp water; and the breadcrumbs mixed with the paprika, garlic powder and oil.
Coat each fish fillet in flour, dip in egg, then press into the crumbs on both sides. Lay on the pan.
Bake 12–15 minutes until the crust is golden and the fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork (145°F). Serve with lemon wedges.

name: Roasted vegetables
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the broccoli, carrots, bell pepper and red onion with the oil, italian seasoning, garlic powder, salt and pepper on a large sheet pan.
Spread in a single layer (use two pans if crowded so they roast instead of steam).
Roast 25–30 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and browned at the edges.

name: Broccoli cheddar soup

ingredients.note: use vegetable broth to keep it vegetarian

steps: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the flour and cook 1 minute, then slowly whisk in the broth and milk.
Add the broccoli and carrots, bring to a gentle simmer (not a hard boil) and cook 15–20 minutes until the broccoli is tender.
Turn the heat to low and stir in the cheese a handful at a time until melted. Season with salt and pepper; blend part of it if you like it smoother.

name: Banana bread
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
Mash the bananas in a large bowl, then stir in the melted butter, sugar, egg and vanilla.
Sprinkle the baking powder, salt and cinnamon if using over the top and stir, then fold in the flour until just combined (a few lumps are fine).
Pour into the pan and bake 55–65 minutes until golden and a toothpick in the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pan 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack before slicing.

name: Peanut butter energy bites
steps: Stir the oats, peanut butter, honey, vanilla, cinnamon if using and salt together in a bowl until evenly combined.
Chill the mixture 20–30 minutes so it is easier to handle.
Roll into 1-inch balls (about 14) with damp hands. Store in a covered container in the fridge up to 1 week.

name: Deviled eggs
steps: Put the eggs in a pot, cover with cold water by an inch and bring to a boil over high heat. Turn off the heat, cover, and let sit 11 minutes until the yolks are fully set and firm.
Move the eggs to ice water for 5 minutes, then peel and halve lengthwise.
Pop the yolks into a bowl and mash with the mayo, mustard, vinegar if using, salt and pepper until smooth.
Spoon or pipe the filling back into the whites and sprinkle with paprika. Keep chilled until serving.
